info.title: PickFu API
info.description:
The PickFu API enables programmatic access to create surveys, retrieve results, and integrate PickFu into your workflows.

## Overview

PickFu helps you get instant consumer feedback through surveys. With the API, you can:

- Create surveys programmatically
- Retrieve survey results and respondent data
- Target specific audiences with demographic traits
- Integrate PickFu into your product development workflow

## Rate Limits

Selected endpoints (currently the CSV export endpoints) enforce per-caller rate limits and return `429 Too Many Requests` when exceeded. See each endpoint description for its specific budget.

## Authentication

All API requests require a Bearer token — either an API key or an OAuth 2.0 access token. See the [Authentication guide](https://www.pickfu.com/docs/developers/authentication) for details.

get.description:
Returns all available audience targeting traits that can be used when creating or updating surveys. Traits allow you to reach specific demographics such as age groups, gender, income levels, shopping habits, and more.

Optionally filter by country code to see traits available in a specific market.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code to filter available traits (e.g. US, GB). Defaults to US traits when omitted.

trait_name.description: Human-readable trait name with category prefix (e.g. "Age: 25-34")

permalink.description: Trait permalink to use in the targeting array when creating or updating surveys

get.description:
Returns all available reporting/demographic breakdown traits that can be applied to surveys. These traits allow you to segment survey results by demographics such as age, gender, income, and more.

Optionally filter by country code to see traits available in a specific market.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code to filter available traits (e.g. US, GB). Defaults to US traits when omitted.

permalink.description: Trait permalink to use in the reporting array when creating or updating surveys

get.summary: Search help articles and PickFu examples
get.description: Searches PickFu content matching the query. Use the `types` parameter to select help, example, case_study, and solution results. Results include titles, descriptions, body text, URLs, and response metadata.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search query for help articles (maximum 500 characters)

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination (positive integer, default: 1)

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results per page (1-100, default: 20)

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated result types: help, example, case_study, solution

body.description: Result content. Help articles up to 8,000 characters return in full. Longer help articles return only the sections that best match the query, in article order, prefixed with a line starting "Excerpt:" that gives the full article URL; "…" marks skipped sections. Example, case study and solution results return their best-matching section.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of surveys with filtering and sorting options. Use query parameters to filter by status, type, country, tags, projects, and more.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by survey status. Comma-separated values: completed, in-progress, unpublished, archived

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by question type. Comma-separated values: head_to_head, ranked, open_ended, click_test, etc.

parameters.name: option_type
parameters.description: Filter by option type (e.g. text, image). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Filter by country codes. Comma-separated (e.g. US,GB,CA).

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Filter by tag IDs — opaque identifiers (tag_<32-hex>) and/or legacy integers, mixed freely. Comma-separated.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Full-text search across survey names and questions

parameters.name: externalId
parameters.description: Exact match on the optional opaque correlation key. Account-scoped. Not a text search.

parameters.name: member_id
parameters.description: Filter by team member ID(s) — opaque identifiers (usr_<32-hex>, as returned by GET /users) and/or legacy integers, mixed freely. Comma-separated.

parameters.name: project_ids
parameters.description: Filter by project GUIDs or numeric IDs. Comma-separated.

parameters.name: published_after
parameters.description: Only include surveys published after this ISO 8601 datetime

status.description: Survey status: completed, in-progress, unpublished, or archived

creatorName.description: Name of the team member who created the survey

externalId.description: Optional opaque correlation key. Omitted when unset. Case-sensitive and byte-exact.

template.description: The template the survey was made from, or null. GET the survey for its constraints.

id.description: Template id (cmb_...), or null when the template can no longer be addressed

post.description:
Creates a new survey in draft status. The survey must be published separately using the publish endpoint.

Each survey contains one or more questions, each with a type (head_to_head, ranked, open_ended, etc.) and optional answer options. You can also specify targeting traits, reporting breakdowns, country, and sample size.

To start from a template instead, send `template` (an id from GET /v1/templates, plus any blanks and options) in place of `questions`. The draft is checked against the template limits before anything is written; a request outside them is a 422 listing every violation with its allowed values.

schema.description: Send exactly one of `questions` (write your own poll) or `template` (build it from a template id returned by GET /v1/templates).

projectId.description: Project GUID (string) or numeric ID to associate with the survey, or null to leave unassigned. Mutually exclusive with `projects`.

projects.description: Project GUIDs (or numeric IDs) to associate the survey with. Mutually exclusive with `projectId`.

tags.description: Tags to attach. Each item has either id (existing tag) or name (find-or-create).

surveyIntent.description: Original intent of the survey as interpreted by AI (max 255 characters)

isMiniPoll.description: Whether to create this survey as a daily mini-poll

externalId.description: Optional opaque correlation key for your own records. Omit when unset. Case-sensitive and byte-exact — send the identical string every time. Many surveys may share the same id. We do not interpret this value.

template.description: Create the survey from a template instead of writing `questions`. A template is one ready-made question with a fixed price per response and fixed limits (question type, option count and kinds, sample sizes, countries, audience). Call GET /v1/templates/{id} first to read its question, blanks, option slots and constraints. The server picks the question type from the template (head_to_head for 2 options or fewer and ranked for 3 or more, where a template offers both). Omitted survey fields come from the template: `sampleSize` its default size, `country` its default country, `name` its title, and `targeting` its preset audience (send the full list to change it, keeping the preset). Its reporting traits always apply, so `reporting` cannot be sent. A request outside the limits is rejected with a 422 listing every violation; nothing is written. Create only: edit the draft afterwards with `questions`.

prompt.description: Replaces the question of a template without blanks, and is required when the template has no question. A template whose question has {{name}} blanks takes `blanks` instead; `prompt` is rejected there.

blanks.description: One value per {{name}} blank in the template's question, keyed by the blank's name. Every blank must be filled.

context.description: Context shown with the question, as text or as a media URL (one, not both). Only for templates that take context.

options.description: The question's options, in the same shape as a question's options. Omit to use the template's preset option values when it has one for every slot.

mockup.description: Either an Amazon product mockup (`type`, `image`, `title`, `price`, …) or a first-party mockup template (`template` with `values`, `import` or both), never both. A template keeps the option a text option: send `value` as well, which is the option's text and fills the template's display field. Every option of a question names the same template, or none does. List the templates and the values each takes with GET /v1/mockup-templates.

template.description: Lookup key of a mockup template from GET /v1/mockup-templates, such as `app-store-page`.

values.description: The template's field values, keyed by field name, as its `valuesSchema` describes. Leave out the display field: it is the option's `value`.

import.description: A store listing that fills the template's values before the survey is saved, for templates whose `importSources` list the store. `values` sent beside it win, so send the fields a store does not provide, such as an App Store subtitle, there. The option's `value` stays its text. Images are copied to PickFu's media CDN as when sent in `values`.

id.description: The app: an App Store link such as https://apps.apple.com/us/app/name/id123456789, or the number after "id".

country.description: Two-letter storefront to read the listing from when the link names none. Defaults to the survey's country.

questions.description: List of questions for the survey. Required unless `template` is sent.

type.description: Question type. Every type except screen_recording automatically collects a required written explanation from each respondent, returned as the response's `explanation` field. Do NOT add a separate open_ended question to capture 'why' — it duplicates the built-in explanation and wastes a question slot (multi-question surveys are priced per question).

prompt.description: Question text prompt (max 255 chars). Every response automatically includes a required written explanation from the respondent for all types except screen_recording — phrase the real question here and PickFu collects the 'why' automatically.

variant.description: Persisted question variant. For likert questions, accepts canonical variant slugs returned by GET.

context.description: Context provided with the question: text, a mediaUrl, or both. With both, text is the caption shown with the image and mediaUrl must be an image URL.

likertScale.description: Likert scale preset. Only honored when type=likert. Defaults to agreement5 (5-point Agreement) if omitted. DEV-3128.

type.description: Question type (head_to_head, ranked, open_ended, click_test, emoji_rating, star_rating, five_second_test, screen_recording, single_select, multi_select, likert, van_westendorp)

variant.description: Question variant for specialized display modes

value.description: Question text

likertScale.description: Likert scale preset, returned for likert questions whose variant matches one of the canonical presets. Null for non-likert questions or legacy likert questions with no recognized variant.

product.description: Product data for product-type options (ASIN or custom mockups)

salePrice.description: Discounted/sale price. null when the product is not on sale.

reviewScore.description: Alias of rating for public API round-trip

numRatings.description: Alias of reviews for public API round-trip

mockupType.description: Product mockup rendering style: serp or listing (product options only)

On update, leaving `mockup` out or sending it back unchanged keeps the page, and `mockup: null` removes the question's template.

context.description: Additional context provided with the question (e.g. a product description or image)

value.description: Context content: the text, or for media the hosted media URL

text.description: Caption shown with the image. Present only on a media context that has one; send it back with the media URL to keep both.

results.description: Aggregated, page-faithful summary of the outcome for this question — the same percentages and ranking shown on the results page. Null for question types without a simple per-option aggregate (open_ended, click_test, likert, five_second_test, screen_recording, round_robin) or before any responses arrive. For ranked questions, `votes` is the final instant-runoff tally the percentage is computed from, and differs from the first-choice count shown beside each option on the page; the winner exceeds 50%.

totalResponses.description: Number of valid responses the percentages are computed against

winningOptionId.description: GUID of the winning option, or null on a tie / before a winner is decided

averageScore.description: Average rating, returned for rating questions only (emoji_rating, star_rating)

options.description: Per-option results, ordered by rank (winner first)

votes.description: Vote count; the final instant-runoff tally for ranked questions

percentage.description: round(votes / totalResponses * 100), matching the results page

isWinner.description: Whether this option is the winner

chosenOption.description: Label of the option chosen by the respondent

selectedOptions.description: Labels of options selected by the respondent for multi-select questions

score.description: Rating score (for emoji_rating, star_rating question types)

ranking.description: Respondent's ranking of options for ranked question types. Each entry pairs a rank (1 = top pick) with the option label.

matchup.description: Head-to-head matchup pairing shown to the respondent

statements.description: Per-statement responses for likert question types. Each entry pairs a statement with the numeric value the respondent picked on the configured scale. DEV-3149.

id.description: GUID of the statement (the question option)

value.description: Numeric value the respondent picked on the Likert scale (1..N for the configured scale)

prices.description: Van Westendorp price-sensitivity responses. Four numeric prices the respondent provided for the four standardized PSM questions.

tooCheap.description: Price at which the product would be so cheap that quality is questionable

bargain.description: Price at which the product would be a bargain

expensive.description: Price at which the product starts to feel expensive but is still worth considering

tooExpensive.description: Price at which the product would be too expensive to consider

value.description: Trait value

ai.description: AI-generated metadata such as summaries and key themes for this question

quotedCreditsCost.description: Post-discount cost in credits, after free credits applied (1 credit = $2 USD)

creditsCostSubtotal.description: Pre-discount cost in credits (1 credit = $2 USD)

discounts.description: Credit-side discount line items, each entry is [label, amountInCredits]. Amounts are denominated in credits so they subtract directly from creditsCostSubtotal

discountsMoney.description: Dollar-side discount line items, each entry is [label, formattedDollarAmount] (e.g. "$20.08")

planRequired.description: Plan tier required for current survey configuration, or null if the current plan is sufficient

priceLines.description: The survey builder's price summary, each entry is [label, formattedDollarAmount] (e.g. ["Head-to-Head: Text Length (+1.2x)", "$10.00"]). Each amount is that line's cost for the whole sample: base price, extra options, text or video length, targeting and reporting. A $0.00 line is included free. The lines come before discounts: they add up to `creditsCostSubtotal` in dollars, and `discountsMoney` takes that down to `amount`

completionEstimate.description: Estimated completion-time bucket for the current audience

bucket.description: Completion-time bucket: SUPER_EASY (<2h), EASY (1-2 days), MEDIUM (up to 2 weeks), HARD (may take longer), MAY_NOT_COMPLETE

estimatedMinutes.description: Estimated completion time in minutes, or null when unavailable

status.description: ready when an estimate exists, pending while computing

A product combo template lists each limit with its allowed and received values; a mockup template lists each option field to change, as a path such as `questions[0].options[1].mockup.values.icon`.

delete.description:
Deletes or archives a survey depending on its state:

- **Draft surveys** (unpublished) are soft-deleted and will no longer appear in listings
- **Published surveys** (with or without responses) are archived — their data is preserved but they are hidden from default listings

This operation is idempotent: deleting an already-archived survey returns 200 with `action: "archived"`.

patch.description:
Updates a draft survey. All fields use replace-all semantics — for example, sending `tags` replaces all existing tags, and sending `questions` replaces all existing questions.

Only surveys in `unpublished` (draft) status can be updated. You can update the name, tags, project, questions, targeting, reporting, country, sample size, and survey intent.

tags.description: Tags to replace all existing tags. Each item has either id or name.

id.description: Existing tag ID — opaque identifier (tag_<32-hex>) or legacy integer

projectId.description: Project GUID (string) or numeric ID to associate, or null to remove project. Mutually exclusive with `projects`.

projects.description: Project GUIDs (or numeric IDs) to associate the survey with. Replace-all semantics. Mutually exclusive with `projectId`.

questions.description: Questions to replace all existing questions (replace-all semantics)

id.description: Question GUID from GET response. Include to update in-place (preserving response data). Omit to create as new.

type.description: Question type. Every type except screen_recording automatically collects a required written explanation from each respondent, returned as the response's `explanation` field. Do NOT add a separate open_ended question to capture 'why' — it duplicates the built-in explanation and wastes a question slot (multi-question surveys are priced per question).

prompt.description: Question text prompt (max 255 chars). Every response automatically includes a required written explanation from the respondent for all types except screen_recording — phrase the real question here and PickFu collects the 'why' automatically.

variant.description: Persisted question variant. For likert questions, accepts canonical variant slugs returned by GET.

likertScale.description: Likert scale preset. Only honored when type=likert. On PATCH, omitting this field leaves the existing scale unchanged. DEV-3128.

context.description: Context provided with the question: text, a mediaUrl, or both (text is then the caption shown with the image, and mediaUrl must be an image URL). Also accepts the {type, value, text?} format from GET responses.

id.description: Option GUID from GET response. Include to update in-place. Omit to create as new.

mockup.description: Either an Amazon product mockup (`type`, `image`, `title`, `price`, …) or a first-party mockup template (`template` with `values`, `import` or both), never both. A template keeps the option a text option: send `value` as well, which is the option's text and fills the template's display field. Every option of a question names the same template, or none does. List the templates and the values each takes with GET /v1/mockup-templates. On update, leaving `mockup` out keeps the option's page, and `null` removes the question's mockup template from every option.

template.description: Lookup key of a mockup template from GET /v1/mockup-templates, such as `app-store-page`.

values.description: The template's field values, keyed by field name, as its `valuesSchema` describes. Leave out the display field: it is the option's `value`.

import.description: A store listing that fills the template's values before the survey is saved, for templates whose `importSources` list the store. `values` sent beside it win, so send the fields a store does not provide, such as an App Store subtitle, there. The option's `value` stays its text. Images are copied to PickFu's media CDN as when sent in `values`.

country.description: Two-letter storefront to read the listing from when the link names none. Defaults to the survey's country.

post.description:
Marks an individual respondent comment as helpful or not_helpful.

Calling this with `rating: "helpful"` records a positive vote.

Calling with `rating: "not_helpful"` flags the response as low-quality. For non-admin users this counts against a per-survey flag cap. Free (pay-as-you-go) survey owners may flag up to 10% of the sample size (rounded up); subscribed (PickFu+/Enterprise) owners have no cap. Returns 409 when the cap is exceeded. When the cap is not exceeded the response — and, on multi-question surveys, all responses from the same respondent — is automatically marked as rejected, the survey's valid-answer count is recalculated, and a previously completed survey may be reopened to collect replacement responses.

The endpoint is upserting: re-rating the same response replaces the previous rating and preserves any existing `comment` when one is not re-supplied. Switching a previous `not_helpful` rating to `helpful` records the new vote but does NOT un-reject the answer that was auto-rejected by the prior flag.

Use `DELETE /v1/responses/{id}/rate` to remove a rating; note that DELETE does NOT un-reject an answer that was rejected by a prior `not_helpful` rating, and removing a flag does free up cap space — repeatedly flagging then deleting can reject more answers than the cap allows without tripping it.

rating.description: Whether the response was helpful or not. "not_helpful" flags the response as low-quality and may auto-reject it; see endpoint description for the full effect.

comment.description: Optional reason or note attached to the rating.

delete.description: Removes a previously-applied helpful / not_helpful rating from a response. Returns 404 if no rating exists. Does not un-reject answers that were auto-rejected by a prior not_helpful rating.

post.description:
Stops a live survey that is currently collecting responses. This is irreversible — the survey will be marked as complete and no further responses will be collected.

### Prerequisites
- Survey must be in `in-progress` status (published and not yet done)
- Stopping a completed or draft survey returns 409 Conflict

Adds more respondents to a completed survey by extending the sample size. The `respondentsAmount` parameter is the **new total** number of respondents (not the number to add).

### Prerequisites
- Survey must be completed (`done` status)
- Panel-sourced surveys only
- Under 1000 total respondents
- Account must have sufficient credits

Use `preview: true` to get a cost estimate without making changes. Credits-only — card payment is not supported via the API.

get.description:
Returns the named boxes (regions) drawn on a click-test question's current image, and how respondents' clicks fall in them.

### Counting
- `mode=first` (default) counts each respondent's first click; `mode=all` counts every click.
- Boxes are half-open: a click on an edge two regions share counts in the right or lower one. A box reaching the image's right or bottom edge includes it.
- Each region and `outside` carry `count`, a whole-percent `share` (summing to 100) and, in `first` mode, a Wilson 95% interval `ci95` in percent.
- `noClearWinner` is a heuristic, not a significance test: true when the two most-clicked regions' intervals overlap, so no region should be called the winner yet.

### Filters
- `traits`: comma-separated trait value permalinks, as on the responses endpoint.
- `startX`, `startY`, `w`, `h`: a drag box as fractions of the image (all four or none). Only respondents with any click inside it are counted.

Regions belong to an image: after the question's image is replaced, `revision` is 0 and `regions` is empty until regions are saved for the new image. A click test without clicks answers zero counts. Returns 422 for a question that is not a click test or has no image.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `first` (default) counts each respondent's first click; `all` counts every click.

parameters.name: startX
parameters.description: Drag-box filter, left edge as a fraction. Send startX, startY, w and h together: only respondents with any click inside the box (edges included) are counted, by their own first click in `first` mode.

parameters.name: startY
parameters.description: Drag-box filter, top edge as a fraction

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: Drag-box filter, width; negative for a box dragged left

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Drag-box filter, height; negative for a box dragged up

parameters.name: traits
parameters.description: Comma-separated trait value permalinks, as on GET /surveys/{id}/responses: only matching respondents are counted. Traits outside the poll's trait set are refused with 400.

put.description:
Saves the whole set of regions for a click-test question's current image as a new revision, and returns it with unfiltered first-click counts. Allowed on draft, live and completed surveys for users who can edit the survey; requires an API key with write permission.

Send the `imagePublicId` and `revision` the GET returned (revision 0 when there is none). Regions are fractions of the image (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h` in 0 to 1), at most 50, with unique keys; they may share an edge but not overlap. Saving regions equal to the current ones creates no revision.

### Errors
- 409 `CLICK_REGIONS_IMAGE_CHANGED`: the question's image was replaced since the GET. Reload and draw the regions again.
- 409 `CLICK_REGIONS_STALE_REVISION`: someone saved since the GET, or a concurrent save won. Reload and reapply.
- Both carry `current: { imagePublicId, revision }`.
- 422 `CLICK_REGIONS_INVALID`: the message names each region to fix (overlap, out of bounds, zero size, duplicate key).

imagePublicId.description: The image the regions were drawn on: `imagePublicId` from the GET. A save for any other image is refused with 409 `CLICK_REGIONS_IMAGE_CHANGED`.

revision.description: The revision being edited: `revision` from the GET, 0 when there is none yet. A save against an older revision is refused with 409 `CLICK_REGIONS_STALE_REVISION`.

key.description: Unique within the set, such as `slot-3`

label.description: Shown to people reading results; null or omitted for none

x.description: Left edge, as a fraction of the image width

y.description: Top edge, as a fraction of the image height

w.description: Width, as a fraction of the image width; above 0

h.description: Height, as a fraction of the image height; above 0

regions.description: The whole set, replacing the current one. Boxes may share an edge but not overlap, and must lie within the image.

get.description:
Returns the aggregated Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter analysis for a van_westendorp question: the four cumulative respondent-price curves (Too cheap / Bargain / Expensive / Too expensive), the four named price intersections (PMC, OPP, IPP, PME), per-bucket histograms, and a confidence signal. Useful when the caller wants the analyzed price points without parsing every respondent's raw quartet themselves.

### Prerequisites
- Question must be a `van_westendorp` type
- Question must have at least one approved response
- Returns 422 for non-VW questions or questions with no approved responses yet

parameters.name: questionId
parameters.description: Question GUID within the survey (must be a van_westendorp question)

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency derived from the survey target country

priceRange.description: Price-axis bounds derived from respondent answers (used by curves + histograms).

curves.description: Cumulative respondent percentages at each price step, one entry per axis price (indices align across all four curves and with priceRange.min..max stepped by priceRange.step).

intersections.description: Named Van Westendorp price points. Ordering invariant: PMC ≤ OPP ≤ IPP ≤ PME.

PMC.description: Point of Marginal Cheapness — tooCheap × expensive intersection (lower bound of acceptable range)

OPP.description: Optimal Price Point — tooCheap × tooExpensive intersection

IPP.description: Indifference Price Point — bargain × expensive intersection (typical market price)

PME.description: Point of Marginal Expensiveness — bargain × tooExpensive intersection (upper bound of acceptable range)

nms.description: Percentage of respondents for whom each price is within their acceptable range — neither too cheap nor too expensive — computed as max(0, 100 − tooCheap − tooExpensive) at each price step (indices align with the curves). Not the full Newton-Miller-Smith purchase-probability model, which requires extra trial questions this question type does not collect.

histograms.description: Per-bucket distributions of respondent prices for each of the four PSM questions.

confidence.description: Quality signal based on respondent count and data spread

get.description:
Returns metadata and download URLs for all export formats associated with a survey: CSV results, PDF reports, and PNG screenshots.

The `csv` block points to the PickFu API CSV proxy endpoint and is only available once the survey has been published and completed. PDF and PNG entries are returned for each rendered language.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute per caller.

available.description: Whether the CSV export is available (the survey must be published and complete)

version.description: CSV export version. v2 is the default and most recent format.

url.description: Authenticated URL to download the CSV results bytes via the PickFu API.

pdf.description: PDF report exports. Each entry corresponds to one rendered language.

url.description: Direct CDN URL to the PDF file

png.description: PNG screenshot exports of the results page. Each entry is one rendered language and may be a preview thumbnail.

url.description: Direct CDN URL to the PNG file

isPreview.description: True when the PNG is a preview thumbnail rather than a full-resolution screenshot

get.description:
Streams the CSV export of survey responses as `text/csv`. Use the `version` query parameter to switch between the v1 and v2 CSV formats — v2 is the default.

Authentication: standard Bearer token, OR a short-lived signed token via the `t` query parameter (issued by `/v1/surveys/{id}/exports`).

### Prerequisites
- Survey must be published and completed
- Returns 409 Conflict if the survey is not yet ready for export
- Returns 502 Bad Gateway if the upstream export service is unavailable

Rate limit: 10 requests per minute per caller.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: CSV export format version. Defaults to v2 (long-form) if omitted.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: Optional short-lived signed token. When present and valid, the request is authenticated by the token instead of the Authorization header. Tokens are issued by the `/v1/surveys/{id}/exports` metadata endpoint.

post.description:
Uploads an image or video to the PickFu CDN. Accepts either a URL (fetched and re-hosted) or base64-encoded data (max 20MB decoded).

YouTube, Vimeo, and Wistia URLs are returned as-is since PickFu embeds them natively.

url.description: HTTPS URL of the media to upload. Mutually exclusive with data.

data.description: Base64-encoded media content. Mutually exclusive with url. Max 20MB.

filename.description: Optional filename hint for the CDN public ID

resourceType.description: Resource type. Auto-detected from URL/content if omitted.

url.description: CDN URL of the uploaded media

embedded.description: True if the URL is an embeddable video platform (YouTube/Vimeo/Wistia) returned as-is

bearerAuth.description: OAuth2 access token obtained via the authorization flow. Include in the Authorization header as: `Bearer {access_token}`
